results: Complete generalized-weight hierarchy of both signed k=2 proper-star codes at every available rank, including the distinct empty-star and p=2 cases.
For every k>=2,q>=3, the first two nonzero codeword weights are 2q+2 and 4q+2, with no intermediate weights.
For every k>=2,q>=3, d3=6q+3 and every optimal three-dimensional subcode is a triangle of minimum stars. Exactly 2^(k+1) binom(p,k-2) binom(q+2,3) optima exist.
A prescribed triple at q>=3 attains 6q deletions exactly when its columns have rank three on an optimal triangle; the larger budgets for failing triples are not classified.
At q=2, d3=15 for k=2,3, while k>=4 has exact prefix (d1,d2,d3,d4,d5)=(6,11,14,15,16). A localized affine cube beats all three-minimum-star spans.
Three, four, and five selectable targets at q=2,k>=4 all need exactly eleven deletions. Explicit nonempty proper-star decoders and naive scalar cost receipts are supplied.
Code results hold for both C-minus and C-plus; original overlap corrections are absorbed only at power-of-two k. No new supplier or kappa is claimed.
